## Function Parse Command

argv into one Command or a usage error.

Behaviour: parseCommand(argv) scans argv left to right. A token starting with "--" is a flag: flags.json "bare" take no value, "valued" take the next token whatever it is; another flag (--x=y too) → "unknown flag: <t>"; a value flag last → "flag <t> needs a value"; a flag twice → "flag <t> given twice", but --component repeats, values in argv order (the first error by argv wins). Other tokens are words naming the command: none → "no command (commands: deck check, plan, run, submit, collect, primer, scout, review, card, accept, init)"; run; plan ("plan --from-scout" with --from-scout); submit; collect; primer; scout; review + two words <base> <head>; card; accept; init; gate; deck check; a first word report → NotYetError "command report is not available yet"; deck add|status|reset|clear → NotYetError "command deck <w> is not available yet"; else "unknown command: <words, space-joined>". An extra word → "unexpected argument: <first extra>". Then in order: a flag the command does not take → "flag <f> does not apply to <command>", in argv order (flags.json "takes": the flags of "every command" plus the command's own). Below I = ^[A-Za-z0-9._-]+$; "<f> ~ P" = a value not matching P → "<f> must match P (got '<v>')", P written out; "need <f>" = no <f> → "missing <f>"; "<f> ≡ I,<what>" = a value split on "," that is not distinct <what> each matching I → "<f> must be distinct <what> joined by \",\" (got '<v>')". card and accept: need --deck, need --id, --id ~ I (accept: an --id holding "," ≡ I,card ids); card done. accept: --from-run ~ I; --model with --from-run → "--model does not apply with --from-run"; --pick without it → "--pick needs --from-run"; without --from-run need --model, --model ~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]+$; --pick ≡ I,answer names; else done (model null with --from-run; fromRun, then pick (names in order), each key only when given). init: need --name, --name ~ I, need --language, not typescript, python or go → "--language must be one of typescript, python, go (got '<v>')", --module ~ ^[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+$, else done (module, templates null when not given). review: fewer than two refs → "review needs two refs: <base> <head>", --scout ~ I, --mutants then --mutant-timeout not a positive integer, else done (mutants null, mutantTimeoutSeconds 120, test null when not given). plan --from-scout: --from-scout ~ I, else done (out null when not given). plan: need --spec; a given --only ≡ I,card ids; --write-probes without --checks → "--write-probes needs --checks", with --out → "--write-probes writes no deck: drop --out"; else done (components [] and map, out null when not given; checks, then only (ids in order), then writeProbes true, each key only when given). collect: need --batch, --batch ~ I, else done. primer done (write: --write given). scout: need --processor, need --issue, --deadline not a positive integer → "--deadline must be a positive integer (got '<v>')", else done (seedFile null, deadlineSeconds null when not given: Main's config gives it). The rest: need --deck; gate: need --stubs, need --refs, --mutants as review's, else done (mutants only when given); run or submit: need --processor; submit done; run: --run-id ~ I; numbers in the order --slice-cap-bytes (deck check), --deadline, --max-cards, --max-retry-batches (run): digits only, ≥ 1 ("<f> must be a positive integer (got '<v>')"), --max-retry-batches ≥ 0 ("must be a non-negative integer"). A failure is {ok: false, error: {error: {code: 4, kind: "UsageError"|"NotYetError", message}}}. Defaults: root ".", pretty false, sliceCapBytes 500000, runId null, deadlineSeconds 2400, maxCards null (the card count), maxRetryBatches 2.

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a). review-session spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance (the mutant runs, each under its timeout) and git's Run Git; Run Mutants writes only through acceptance's Restore Snapshot; Review Command is the reviewer layer's one node:fs file (the record, the map and scout.json read, the review written), the environment a parameter, no clock and no model call (P14b). debt spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance and git's Run Git, reads the deck file, the card's files and the run archive through node:fs, no clock and no model call; the environment is a parameter (P17). scaffold reads the template folders and writes the new project through node:fs (node:url only to find the package root from its own module file), spawns nothing, reads no clock and no environment (P18).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

## Function Probe Skeleton

The probe text of a code card with no probe, one failing test per example of its Functions.

Behaviour: probeSkeleton({id, profile, functions, targets}) → string; functions = the card's Card Criterion functions ({name, examples}, in order), targets = its plan card's. The lines joined by "\n", plus a last "\n". C1 = "// Probe of card '<id>', written by morph plan --write-probes: one test per example of its Functions.", C2 = "// Write each body from its example; until you do, it fails.". An example's value lines, in order: "given: <given>", "ref: <ref>" only when ref is not null, "when: <when>", "then: <then>", each value with every run of whitespace collapsed to one space, trimmed. Per Function in order, per its example n from 1, one test. The go profile: "package <pkg>", "", C1, C2, "", `import "testing"`; per test "", `func TestProbe<X>Example<n>(t *testing.T) {` (X = Probe Names' pascalName(name)), a tab + "// " + each value line, a tab + `t.Fatal("probe <id>: write <name> example <n>")`, "}". pkg: the first of language's codeTargets(profile, targets) up to its last "/"; no such target or no "/" → "main", else that directory's text after its last "/" ("calc/clamp_value.go" → "calc", "a/b/c.go" → "b"). Any other profile: C1, C2, `import { expect, test } from "vitest";`; per test "", `test("<name> example <n>", () => {`, two spaces + "// " + each value line, two spaces + `throw new Error("probe <id>: write <name> example <n>");`, "});". No example in any Function: one test in their place, go "", `func TestProbeOwn(t *testing.T) {`, a tab + "// the record gives no example: write the probe's own tests", a tab + `t.Fatal("probe <id>: no record example")`, "}"; else "", `test("<id> probe", () => {`, two spaces + "// the record gives no example: write the probe's own tests", two spaces + `throw new Error("probe <id>: no record example");`, "});". Probe Names reads every title back: checkProbeNames of a skeleton, strict, own = its functions' Example Counts, is [].

## Function Plan Command

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Strict TypeScript: tsconfig strict, ESM, no `any`; every module compiles with tsc --noEmit.
- One Document Out: Every command prints exactly one JSON document on stdout and nothing else; the human log goes to stderr.
- Deterministic Core: cards and compiler give byte-identical results for the same inputs: no clock, no randomness, no environment reads. acceptance is bound only in its pure parts (Snapshot Targets, Build Attempt Diff): Run Acceptance spawns a shell and its only timer is the child's timeout; env and the timeout are parameters, never process.env (06.10, P3). processor reads the environment only in Read Registry; Assemble Request, Read Response, Stub Answer, Assemble Batch and Read Batch are pure of clock and network; the transport and its sleep are parameters of Send Generation and Send Batch (P4, P11). git spawns only in Run Git, synchronously, with the child's environment given whole as a parameter; it reads no process.env and no clock of its own (P6). cli touches the process only in its entry src/cli.ts: the environment, the working directory, the clock and the output streams reach main() as parameters, and the environment reaches the processor only through Read Registry (P7). language is pure data and pure functions: no clock, no environment, no file system, no child process; node:path is its only Node module; its shell lines are text (P8). contour reads no file, no clock and no environment: it parses the text it is given; the package yaml is imported in Parse Document alone (P9). planner reads no file, no clock and no environment: the cli reads the record and the map and passes which files exist as a function; node:path is its only Node module (P10a). builder reads no file, no clock and no environment: the caller passes the checks, the cards, the profile and the texts of the guard, the locator and the probes; node:path is its only Node module (P10b). primer reads files and spawns git (git's gitOk, the environment a parameter) only in Primer Command, the clock only there through deps.now; Read Runs, Read Story and Render Primer are pure functions of what they are given, no network anywhere (P12a). scout reads no clock, no environment and no network and spawns nothing: Parse Turn, Spend Budget and Seed From Ownership are pure; Cage Path and Run Tool reach the file system only through the ScoutFs parameter (realpath, readFile); elapsed time is a parameter; node:path is its only Node module (P13a). scout-session reaches the model only through the processor's Send Generation and the clock only through deps.now; Run Scout reads the tree through the ScoutFs parameter; Scout Command and Plan From Scout are the scout layer's two node:fs files (git through gitOk and runGit, node:crypto for the sha256 in Scout Command), the environment a parameter (P13b). reviewer's checks (Find Obligations, Check Envelope, Check Guardrails, Plan Mutants, Render Findings) are pure functions of the record, git's outputs and the texts they are given: no file, no clock, no environment, no child process, no Node module (P14a). review-session spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance (the mutant runs, each under its timeout) and git's Run Git; Run Mutants writes only through acceptance's Restore Snapshot; Review Command is the reviewer layer's one node:fs file (the record, the map and scout.json read, the review written), the environment a parameter, no clock and no model call (P14b). debt spawns only through acceptance's Run Acceptance and git's Run Git, reads the deck file, the card's files and the run archive through node:fs, no clock and no model call; the environment is a parameter (P17). scaffold reads the template folders and writes the new project through node:fs (node:url only to find the package root from its own module file), spawns nothing, reads no clock and no environment (P18).
- Node Only: Runtime dependencies: Node 20 built-ins and the package `yaml` (the record reader), nothing else; dev dependencies pinned exactly, no ^ or ~.

Guardrails:
- No Network In Tests: tests/setup.ts makes fetch, XMLHttpRequest, WebSocket and net.connect throw "network blocked in tests"; only the processor's own transport is mocked.
- No Shell Outside Acceptance: child processes are spawned only by Run Acceptance, the git module (in Run Git alone, P6) and the processor's none; everything else is pure.
- Frozen Tree During Run: while a run is in flight no file outside the cards' targets and .morph/ changes; a changed declared input discards the answer unread.

Callee Probe Names: The example titles of a probe, and every one the record does not give or the probe lacks.
Behaviour: pascalName(name) = language's nameWords(name), each word with its first letter upper-cased, joined ("Percent Of" → "PercentOf", "MCP mount" → "McpMount"). probeTitles(profile, text, names) → Probe Title[] in line order, text split on "\n". The go profile: a line starting "func TestProbe" + X + "Example" + n + "(" (X one or more of [A-Za-z0-9_], the longest that fits; n digits) → {function: the first of names whose pascalName is X, letter case ignored ("PMTools" is "PM Tools"), else X; n: Number(n)}. Any other profile: a line whose first non-blank characters (spaces, tabs) are "test(" or "it(", then optional spaces, then a quote (", ' or a backquote), the title running to the next same quote on the line; a title "<F> example <n>" or "<F> example <n>:<rest>" (F at least one character, n digits) → {function: F, n}; every other title is the probe's own test, skipped. checkProbeNames({id, path, profile, text, own, record, strict}) → string[]; own and record are Example Counts ({name, count}); titles = probeTitles(profile, text, record names then own names). A title met twice (an example split over several tests) counts once. strict: per own entry in order, the numbers 1..count no title gives, ascending → "card '<id>': probe <path> lacks <F> example <the numbers joined by ', '> (the record gives <count>)"; then the titles that are not (an own name, 1 ≤ n ≤ its count), grouped by function in order of first appearance, numbers distinct ascending → "card '<id>': probe <path> names <F> example <numbers>, not an example of its Functions (<own names joined by ', ', or none>)". Not strict: no lacks lines; the titles whose function is no record name or whose n is outside 1..count, grouped the same → "card '<id>': probe <path> names <F> example <numbers>, which the record does not give". The lacks lines come before the names lines.
